violations.why: Timer_C (prio 4) can preempt Timer_A's non-atomic increment, and its write is lost.
Reset ISR (prio 5) can preempt the increment's read-modify-write and its reset is overwritten.
Force ISR (prio 3) preempts A's increment, and one of the increments is lost.
Timer_C can write timerCount between A's increment and its check, so the check sees a different value.
Reset ISR can zero timerCount between A's increment and its check.
Force ISR can increment timerCount between A's write and its check, so the ==1 test fails.
Timer_C can overwrite timerCount between B's write and its check.
Reset ISR can zero timerCount between B's write and its check, so the check fails.
Force ISR can increment timerCount between B's write and its check.
Reset ISR (prio 5) can preempt Timer_C between its write and its check.
Timer_C (prio 4) can preempt Force's increment, and its write is lost.
Reset ISR can preempt Force's increment, and the reset is overwritten.
